findings.title: Conduct-indexed punishment
findings.claim: The punishment of the one who does wrong is one arm of a conduct-indexed distribution: the surrounding pericope pairs it with good treatment and with recompense and ease for belief joined to sound action, while the punishment itself remains punitive.
findings.mechanism: The focus forms for wrongdoing and punishment meet the prior punishment-or-good-treatment choice and the parallel response to sound action. That contact changes the reading from an isolated grant of punitive power to a two-sided response organized by the person's conduct.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the focus begins with the person who does wrong and why its punishment is framed as one selected response within a paired policy.
findings.containment: The ordinary meaning of punishment for wrongdoing remains intact. The supplied parallel clauses support a conduct-indexed relation here, without turning this narrative pairing into a general legal code or deciding that the clauses are more than the packet establishes.

epistemic.reason: Exact Arabic anchors and the full HFT trace are supplied, but the conduct-policy arrow is attributed contextual inference from a legacy-unbound record.

findings.title: Delegated and bounded authority
findings.claim: The return of the wrongdoer to his Lord places the ruler's sanction inside a delegated and temporary jurisdiction: capacity is granted, authority is attributed to the Lord, and the ruler's strongest protective work remains under an appointed limit.
findings.mechanism: The focus's passive return to rabbihi meets the supplied empowerment, repeated Lord-attribution, mercy, appointed promise, and demolition traces. Their contact changes the ruler's punishment from self-grounded sovereignty to a provisional exercise whose final ownership and consequence remain with the Lord.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the phrase 'to his Lord' as a limit on the ruler's jurisdiction, not only as the next destination in the narrative.
findings.containment: The ruler's punishment remains real and imposed in the focus. This finding qualifies its jurisdiction as delegated and provisional; it does not claim that every later barrier detail directly determines the first sanction, and the packet's alternative remains live.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies exact anchors and an attributed multi-step HFT trace; the jurisdictional limitation is a qualified contextual inference rather than a direct lexical gloss.

branch_activations.carrier: The empowerment form at 18:84 is attributed with supplying the capacity and means by which the ruler can act.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The focus passively returns the wrongdoer to his Lord after the ruler's first treatment.
branch_activations.activation: Granted capacity meets the jurisdictional return, making the ruler's action readable as delegated rather than self-originating.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The punishment is administered through capacity that the pericope presents as received.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not deny the ruler's agency or claim that every exercise of his power is described in 18:84.

findings.title: Punishment as protective restraint
findings.claim: The first punishment can carry a protective-restraint aspect that removes the wrongdoer's ability to continue disorder, while the Lord's later punishment remains explicitly severe.
findings.mechanism: The focus distinguishes an unqualified first punishment from the later named terrible punishment. The pericope's corruption, breach-blocking, repaired boundary, and mercy supply a concrete protective operation that meets the first verb without dissolving the final punitive noun.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see a difference between stopping harmful agency and the separately specified severe consequence, rather than flattening both occurrences into one undifferentiated act.
findings.containment: The ordinary punitive reading remains present for both occurrences. The protective restraint is a contextual resonance for the first occurrence; the live alternative that the barrier episode is unrelated remains visible.

epistemic.reason: The exact pericope anchors and both punishment occurrences are supplied, but the transfer from physical barrier to penal restraint is attributed contextual inference.

findings.title: A linked transfer of the case
findings.claim: The ayah traces the wrongdoer's case through linked custody: a local sanction is followed by passive return to the proper authority and then by a further consequence.
findings.mechanism: The repeated pericope formula of following a means supplies movement through successive stations, while the focus's thumma separates the first treatment from passive return and the following punishment. The contact changes the ayah from a static list into a relay.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the temporal and procedural handoff carried by thumma and the passive return, rather than hearing three penalties as one flat sequence.
findings.containment: The ordinary sequential narrative remains intact. The custody language is an attributed procedural resonance, and the packet leaves open the alternative that the repeated means language is geographical narration without juridical force.

epistemic.reason: The focus and context occurrences are exact, while the procedural custody arrow is attributed inference from their sequence.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The case moves through connected stages rather than ending with the first treatment.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus presents a relay from local action to transferred authority and final consequence.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not add an unstated human institution or decide that the narrative is juridical in every respect.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Geçişli kullanımda bir etken, şeyi yerine, sahibine veya bağlı olduğu merciye geri gönderir.

findings.title: Exposure as an exploratory penalty image
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the first punishment can also appear as exposure or withdrawal of cover, because its punishment form meets the later scene of a people left without a covering between them and the sky; the final named punishment remains severe.
findings.mechanism: The first focus punishment is still unqualified when it meets the supplied 18:90 occurrence whose defining condition is the absence of sky-cover. That contact adds vulnerability through exposure while the later cognate noun and adjective preserve ordinary punitive pain.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see punishment as more than a positive blow: the first act may also remove protection and leave the wrongdoer exposed before the explicit final penalty.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory, form-distant resonance. The ordinary painful-punishment reading controls the focus, and the exposure image does not claim that the ayah specifies a literal uncovered scene or replaces the final severe punishment.

epistemic.reason: The focus occurrence and the 18:90 covering occurrence are exact, but the HFT record itself marks the cross-branch contact as exploratory and form-distant.

findings.title: Painful restoration of order
findings.claim: Exploratorily, being returned to the Lord can also place the wrongdoer inside the completion of an order violated by wrongdoing, an order whose restoration can still take the expressly painful form named by the ayah.
findings.mechanism: The focus joins the wrongdoing form to rabbihi as the destination of return. The supplied repair-and-completion sense of the Lord, the repaired boundary, and mercy in 18:95 and 18:98 meet that relation and add restoration of violated order beside the focus's explicit punishment.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold return as more than transfer to a stronger punisher: it can also open a repair-of-order image that remains compatible with painful consequence.
findings.containment: The severe punishment remains stated and recoverable. Restoration here means completion of violated order, not automatic benevolence, forgiveness, or denial of pain; the reading is exploratory because the repair mechanism comes through contextual analogy.

epistemic.reason: The focus carriers and contextual repair and mercy anchors are supplied, while the movement from Lordship and wrongdoing to painful restoration is explicitly attributed as exploratory inference.
